alex_sales: Heads-up — Acme POC is hitting intermittent slow TTFT spikes during demo runs. Customer is nervous and asking for a short-term SLA to keep the deal moving. cc @sara_se @tom_runtime @anna_security :eyes:

alex_sales: Symptoms: TTFT p50 ~1.1s but p95 jumps to 5-6s on bursts. Observed high KV cache miss rate (~82%). Also saw periodic 429s. Need quick triage and an estimate for a 2-week dedicated pool (they'll pay).

caroline_cust: adding sample from this morning — user session stuck waiting ~6s, log excerpt attached below. Not changing app behavior for POC.

caroline_cust: ```
[2026-02-27T10:14:02Z] req_id=abcd1234 start=0.010s model=vicuna-13b-8k tokens_in=120 tokens_out=24 KV_CACHE_HIT=false
[2026-02-27T10:14:02Z] step=decode p50=1.02s p95=5.87s
[2026-02-27T10:14:02Z] error_rate=0.0 rate_limit=429? no
KV_CACHE_MISS_RATIO=0.82
```

caroline_cust: workload: chat assistant, avg seq len 120, peak concurrency ~40, sustained ~300 rps during demo scripts.

sara_se: thanks — couple quick hypotheses: 1) batching head-of-line blocking (large batches being assembled before dispatch) 2) prefix/KV cache not matching keys (cache miss churn) 3) occasional rate-limiter spikes causing retries that look like slow TTFT.

sara_se: quick wins to try now (non-disruptive):
- reduce max_batch_size from 32 -> 12
- reduce batch_window_ms from 50 -> 15 (dispatch smaller batches faster)
- enable prefix cache TTL keep-alive (300s) and increase cache_capacity if possible

sara_se: CLI to apply to their pooled run (can do on Hosted):
```bash
redwood run update --pool acme-poc --set batch_window_ms=15 --set max_batch_size=12 --set prefix_cache.enabled=true --set prefix_cache.ttl=300 --set prefix_cache.capacity=512
```

tom_runtime: +1 to sara. Also important: the cache miss ratio suggests the cache keys don't line up. Check that the client isn't randomizing whitespace or adding ephemeral IDs into the prompt prefix. If the session id is part of the prefix key, that will kill hit rate.

tom_runtime: if you can't change prompts, enable "align_prompt_truncation" and use a canonicalization hook so keys are normalized. Example config snippet we use internally: 
```json
{"kv_cache": {"prefix_key":"session_id|sha256(truncate(normalize(prefix),1024))","heuristics":{"align_truncation":true}}}
```

tom_runtime: Also watch for request fanout from their test harness — 40 concurrent UI sessions with 300 rps burst can cause transient token-latency spikes if autoscaling hasn't stabilized.

alex_sales: can Eng spin the CLI changes now on hosted POC? Customer is waiting on this evening demo.

sara_se: I can push the config to their pool now — doing it in canary (10% of traffic) first, then promote after 10m metrics look good.

deploy-bot: deploy started for pool=acme-poc, change_id=chg-20260227-01

deploy-bot: deploy finished for pool=acme-poc, change_id=chg-20260227-01 :white_check_mark:

sara_se: canary looks OK at first glance. p50 stable, p95 dropped from ~5.8s -> ~2.0s on canary nodes. Cache miss ratio on canary dropped to ~28%. Will continue to monitor for 20m.

anna_security: quick security note from the questionnaire — Acme requires EU-only residency and customer-managed KMS for keys. For demo traffic, are we storing any customer text in long-term logs? If so, need to redact or use Private offering.

alex_sales: they want EU only in production but are fine for POC if we mask logs. Sara — can we mask prompt content in logs for the POC?

sara_se: yes — we can enable log redaction for the pool and route telemetry to a restricted project. That avoids needing a Private deployment for demo. I'll toggle redaction and confirm.

finance_bot: Ballpark for a 2-week dedicated pool (4x A10G-equivalent, reserved short term): ~$18k-$24k, depending on burst SLA and 99th percentile latency targets. If they pay for month that drops ~10%.

alex_sales: finance — can you produce a quote by EOD if we confirm dedicated pool? Need procurement to start.

finance_bot: will draft and post here by 18:00 UTC.

caroline_cust: we ran the canary script again — looks much better! p95 dropped to ~2.1s across the board. Great job. :tada:

tom_runtime: follow-up items: 1) instrument KV cache key distribution and surface histogram (we need to prove keys are normalized) 2) add a short-lived Dedicated pool if they want guaranteed latency during sales demo 3) put a retry budget and backoff in client to avoid 429 cascades.

alex_sales: plan/owners: Sara -> finish redaction + promote changes; Tom -> KV key histograms + heuristics; Finance -> quote for 2-week dedicated; Anna -> confirm redaction satisfies questionnaire; Caroline -> confirm demo script this evening.

alex_sales: Thanks everyone — I'm keeping the customer in the loop. Will update once finance quote is in.

caroline_cust: confirming demo tonight at 20:00 UTC. With the canary changes perf looks stable, thanks! :thumbsup:
